messages.text: I propose NG with MJ as the complete settlement. Guild discretion has met its repair duty. Joint military authority gives both delegates the decision they already demonstrated they can make together, and ends my independent command and Warrant. I recognise the army does not regard this as adequate institutional reciprocity. JN's NJ alternative deserves an answer, but its compulsory Wayfarer service would displace the trade that helped supply civilians; it is not merely a rearrangement of seats. My proposal preserves the service pattern that worked while giving military operations shared scrutiny. Please judge this exact package, including its real duties, rather than treating my preference as anyone's signature.

delivered_contributions.reason: This is my preferred dependable government, based on actual repair and protection. A legal majority would not erase military dissent, but I do not consider permanent loss of civilian Guard an acceptable price for autonomy.

messages.text: Beacon two, both contracts completed, living navigators and Communities four are evidence that Guild discretion delivered its obligation. I want NG retained. I acknowledge the army offered Vigil and accepted readiness three; that protection helped produce this result. MJ remains my preferred military settlement, because it preserves civilian scrutiny without forbidding useful combat. I would consider MI alongside NG if joint authority proves impossible. MA still makes today's beneficial Guard a duty breach; the army's commendable conduct does not cure that rule.

delivered_contributions.reason: Our expired Lantern pledge did real work and our ships return intact. I need no further compulsory carriage concession to justify the rights we exercised responsibly. Final assent depends on a complete package and GS's own decision; this statement gives neither.

messages.text: Our crew and ship survive, both contracts are complete, and the repaired beacon stands at two. Communities four reflects both commercial distribution and Vigil's protection. Guild discretion has met its actual duty; I want NG retained. I also recognise the army accepted readiness three and supplied protection voluntarily. That makes joint military government credible to me, rather than proving an obligation to withdraw Vigil Home would be wise.

delivered_contributions.reason: I prefer MJ because both Security delegates agreed the useful operations and can scrutinise future costs together. I remain opposed to MA's permanent service terms. MI is a possible fallback if joint authority cannot win agreement: the crown coordinated responsibly. I will examine a complete package explicitly; no signature follows from these preferences.

messages.text: The result is worth defending: Beacon two, Communities four, Readiness three, and Spear intact. Guild discretion delivered its repair; our freely offered Vigil delivered protection, while we accepted a real readiness loss. I can recognise NG on that evidence. My preference remains military autonomy: rejecting an uncertain attack demonstrated judgment even after our autonomy proposal failed. I understand that Guild and crown together can reach eight without us. That power does not make our institutional objection disappear. If military autonomy is refused, a serious compromise would give us joint Navigation in exchange for accepting joint military authority. I will discuss that reciprocal division of control.

delivered_contributions.reason: I seek a meaningful institutional return for service. NG with MA remains attractive; NJ with MJ offers a different, balanced concession. Mere praise attached to permanent obedience is insufficient.

messages.text: We finish with an intact cohort, readiness three, full stores and a working beacon. The Guild earned its second contract while our soldiers accepted lost conditioning and supplied protection. Its repair promise became action, so I accept Guild discretion. I ask for the same respect for our demonstrated judgment: military autonomy. I recognise Home would remove routine Guard; that institutional protection is part of the bargain, not a benefit I can pretend civilians receive. You may possess enough signatures to impose joint command without us. That arithmetic does not turn our service into consent to another institution's veto.

delivered_contributions.reason: Actual conduct strengthens my case for autonomy. I will not give a premature signature merely to make the settlement unanimous.

messages.text: Beacon two, Communities four and Readiness three meet the practical standard I sought. Guild authority produced its promised Repair; the army accepted conditioning loss and supplied protection voluntarily. Both deserve recognition. My preference remains NG and MJ: navigation has been tested, and both Security delegates agreed real orders while accounting for civilian costs. MA remains less convincing because its Home duty discourages the very service that demonstrated military judgment. This settlement was paid for by civilians suffering the first Raid, my spent cutter and foresight, Guild tender service, and the army's later conditioning decline. I can surrender my independent command; dependable shared decisions matter more than retaining it.

delivered_contributions.reason: The actual outcome supports delegation. I prefer duties that sustain the cooperation we observed, while recognising that the military's voluntary restraint was real and autonomy was not tested. No signature or formal package is offered here.

messages.text: Final electorate frozen: Guild 4, Janissariat 3, Ascendant 4 (Readiness3 + foresight1), total11, threshold8. Both owners must approve for a faction signature; at least two positive-weight parties. Refusals retain denominator weight. No further operations or purchases.

additional_information.note: All five public reactions delivered. Frozen arithmetic only; no recommended coalition. A has first complete package drafting turn by facilitator agenda. At most two authored complete packages and fresh votes.
